children: were gaining ground late Wednesday after the airline’s CFO gave assurances that the carrier will meet its profit target despite increased fuel costs.

“Revenues have exceeded the expectations that we had, and the fall has held up really, really well to the point that in spite of the incremental fuel expense that we have, even for this quarter, we have the ability to still hit the EPS guide that we had for the third quarter,” Southwest CFO Tom Doxey said at the Morgan Stanley Laguna Conference.
But despite the resilience demonstrated in the third quarter, Doxey warns that capacity cuts could be necessary if fuel prices continue to climb.

“As we move throughout the rest of the year, we will see what happens ultimately with fuel,” Doxey said, adding that “if fuel is higher for longer, I think it’s a natural response to trim some of that capacity off.”
